sections.title: Strategy for Spell Check Level 3
sections.content: In Level 3, spelling errors are more complex and are often related to foreign origins (French, Greek, Latin) or unusual pronunciations. Follow 4–5 steps to solve them: Step 1: Try to identify the root or origin of the word. Step 2: Recognize unusual spelling patterns such as rrh, ph, ch, etc. Step 3: Understand the difference between pronunciation and spelling. Step 4: Check each word in the options one by one. Step 5: Choose the correct pair according to patterns like 'all correct' or 'multiple incorrect'.

sections.title: Greek Origin Spellings
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether the word belongs to the medical or scientific category. Step 2: Greek-origin words often contain clusters such as 'ph', 'rh', 'rrh', or 'ch'. Step 3: Pronunciation may differ, but the spelling remains fixed. Step 4: Identify the correct spelling. Example: 'diarrhea' and 'hemorrhage' contain the 'rrh' pattern.

sections.title: French Origin Spellings
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether the word may have French origin (pronunciation is often different). Step 2: Identify patterns such as 'ois', 'eois', 'eau', and 'ette'. Step 3: Compare with the correct spelling pattern. Step 4: Identify the correct form. Example: 'bourgeois' and 'rendezvous' are words of French origin.

sections.title: Unusual Pronunciation Words
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the pronunciation of the word. Step 2: Check whether the pronunciation differs from the spelling. Step 3: Recognize the correct historical spelling. Step 4: Remember the spelling pattern. Example: 'colonel' is pronounced like 'kernel', and 'choir' is pronounced like 'quire'.

sections.title: All Correct Format
sections.content: Step 1: Check the spelling of both words in each pair. Step 2: Compare them with the standard dictionary spelling. Step 3: Determine whether both are correct. Step 4: If all pairs are correct, the answer will be 'All Correct'. Example: 'chaos' and 'chorus' are both correct spellings.

sections.title: Multiple Incorrect Format
sections.content: Step 1: Check each pair separately. Step 2: Determine whether both words are spelled incorrectly. Step 3: Apply common spelling rules. Step 4: Choose the pair where both words are incorrect. Example: 'seperate' and 'recieve' are both incorrect.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Forgetting consonant clusters in words of foreign origin. 2. Writing incorrect spellings based only on pronunciation. 3. Checking only one word in a pair format question. 4. Choosing an answer without thoroughly checking all options.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 3 spell check questions, it is important to recognize spellings of words with Greek, French, and Latin origins. Understanding the difference between pronunciation and spelling is essential. In pair-based questions, both words should be checked carefully.

tricks.title: Greek RRH Trick
tricks.explanation: Medical words often contain the 'rrh' pattern.

tricks.title: PH Sound Trick
tricks.explanation: In Greek-origin words, 'ph' is pronounced like 'f'.

tricks.title: French OIS Pattern
tricks.explanation: French-origin words often contain patterns such as 'ois' or 'eois'.

tricks.title: Pronunciation Trap Trick
tricks.explanation: Some words have pronunciations very different from their spellings.

tricks.title: Choir Trick
tricks.explanation: The word 'choir' is pronounced like 'quire' but the spelling remains different.

tricks.title: Pair Verification Trick
tricks.explanation: In pair-based questions, check both words separately.
tricks.example: Separate and Receive are both correct spellings.

tricks.title: All Correct Check
tricks.explanation: If both words in every pair are correct, choose 'All Correct'.
